Midair collisions happen frighteningly often. Not enough to change the 'safest means of travel' title, but enough that it makes you wonder how it could happen at all.

Whenever a midair collision happens, it's because the pilots weren't aware that the other aircraft was in the area. One really common way it happens is when a low-wing plane (which has bad downward vision because the low wing blocks the pilot's vision) descends into a high-wing plane (which has bad upward vision for the same reason).

In this case, it almost certainly had something to do with the upper pilot being distracted by something the skydivers were doing and the lower pilot being unaware that the upper plane is even there.

There are some technologies that are still being installed on small airplanes that communicate directly with other planes in the area to help avoid collisions.
